header: The four things a paper rota cannot do
lead: Marlbrook Roster was built with duty managers rather than for them, and these are the arguments they make to their own head office.

items.title: The rules are checked while you plan, not afterwards
items.text: Rest periods, maximum weekly hours, minor protection and the terms in each individual contract are tested as the shift lands. A plan that would breach one of them cannot be published, and the reason is shown on the shift itself rather than in a report somebody reads on Monday.

items.title: Everyone works from the same published week
items.text: Once a week goes out, staff see it in the app and any later change arrives as a notification with the old and the new time side by side. The photograph of the whiteboard, taken on a Thursday and still circulating on Sunday, stops being anybody's source of truth.

items.title: Hours arrive at payroll already reconciled
items.text: Clock-in data, approved corrections, absence and premium rates are combined into one monthly figure per employee. What the payroll bureau receives is a file, not a spreadsheet somebody retyped from three others on the last afternoon of the month.

items.title: Cost is visible before the week is committed
items.text: Each draft carries its wage cost against the branch budget and against the same week last year. An area manager can see which of eleven sites is drifting while the plan can still be changed, instead of after the month has closed.
